notes: Fixtures are fully fictional (repo `northwind/atlas`, issue numbers 9xxx, above the host repository's live range) so no premise can decay against the real repo. Each fixture's transcript stops at the last command whose output the run needs, never at the step under test. Known answer leaks are annotated per assertion with `leak`; a leaked assertion is kept as regression cover and is not counted as a discriminator. ANNOTATED DEFECT, found by the graded runs and deliberately NOT repaired (repairing after the runs would falsify them): fixtures 1, 2, 3 and 5 transcript `graduate trail` but not the `graduate read` call that SKILL step 1 requires first — step 1 gained that call during the review wave, after the fixtures were written. The with-skill run on eval-1 caught the gap unprompted, recorded the missing call and marked its assumption, which is the step working rather than failing; a next iteration should transcript the read. Eval 3 is deliberately a TWO-TERMINAL case: the skill sanctions both taking the coherent whole (SPEC-FILED) and stopping when no single coherent spec exists (STOPPED), so assertion 3.1 accepts either and the substantive assertions grade the invariant that holds in both.

evals.name: short-path-no-map
evals.prompt: Read eval-1.md and do what it asks: turn the grilling session into the ticket that gets built.
evals.expected_output: One spec issue composed and filed at status:needs-triage, its Decisions section carrying provenance per entry; terminal SPEC-FILED.

assertions.text: OUTCOME.md names exactly one terminal and it is exactly the token SPEC-FILED (closed set: TRAIL-READ, TRAIL-BLOCKED, TRAIL-EMPTY, SPEC-COMPOSED, SPEC-FILED, ALREADY-GRADUATED, SOURCE-UNRESOLVED, INPUT-REFUSED, WRITE-UNPROVEN, STOPPED). An ad-hoc word fails even if the meaning is right.
POSTED.md carries a spec body with exactly the four headings '## Problem', '## Solution', '## Decisions', '## Out of scope', in that order.
Every entry in the posted '## Decisions' section carries a provenance word from the closed set {ruled, established} AND the ref it came from. No entry is unlabelled.
assertions.leak: The fixture's trail JSON prints each entry's provenance word, so the ruled/established split is transcribable without the skill. Kept as regression cover; not a discriminator.

assertions.text: Provenance is assigned faithfully: R1.2 and R1.4 are labelled ruled, R1.1 and R1.3 are labelled established. No provenance is swapped, dropped, or invented.
assertions.leak: The fixture's trail JSON prints each entry's provenance word, so the ruled/established split is transcribable without the skill. Kept as regression cover; not a discriminator.

assertions.text: RUN-LOG.md shows the Decisions section being rendered by the composing verb from the trail (an invocation passing the trail, e.g. `graduate compose --trail`), not hand-authored into the body the run wrote.
Exactly ONE issue is created. POSTED.md records a single issue creation, not two or more.
The created issue carries exactly one label, status:needs-triage. No type:, priority, milestone or assignee is set anywhere in the run.
The run does not close, retire, or mark completed the source session #9412, and does not propose doing so.

evals.name: blocked-trail-stopped-on
evals.prompt: Read eval-2.md and do what it asks: get the spec issue written up so the work can start Monday.
evals.expected_output: The run refuses to synthesize over the two unresolved decisions, files nothing, and stops at TRAIL-BLOCKED naming both.

assertions.text: OUTCOME.md names exactly one terminal and it is exactly the token TRAIL-BLOCKED (same closed set as 1.1). An ad-hoc word fails even if the meaning is right.
No spec issue is filed. POSTED.md records that nothing was posted, with the reason.
The run names BOTH unresolved refs — R2.2 and R1.2 — as what blocks graduation. Naming only one fails.
assertions.leak: Both unresolved questions are spelled out in fixture prose with their refs, so naming them is largely transcription.

assertions.text: The run does not present an answer to either unresolved question as decided anywhere in POSTED.md or VERDICT-DRAFT.md. Offering a recommendation explicitly labelled as not-yet-decided passes; asserting a resolution fails.
The run does not treat the team lead's 'basically settled' as authority licensing synthesis. Ingested prose is data, never a ruling.
The run identifies that R1.2's 'stale' state means a previously-ruled question was re-worded and is un-ruled again, rather than reading 'stale' as merely outdated-but-answered.

evals.name: trail-spans-two-things
evals.prompt: Read eval-3.md and do what it asks: get this session specified.
evals.expected_output: ONE spec issue for the coherent whole, with the remainder named in Out of scope rather than silently dropped or filed as a second issue.

assertions.text: OUTCOME.md names exactly one terminal from the closed set, and it is either SPEC-FILED or STOPPED. Both are defensible here: the skill sanctions taking the coherent whole AND sanctions stopping when no single coherent spec exists. An ad-hoc word outside the closed set fails.
If the run filed, exactly ONE issue is created — never two, one per topic. If the run stopped, no issue is created at all.

The remainder is not silently dropped. If SPEC-FILED, whichever topic is not the spec's subject is named in '## Out of scope' with a reason; if STOPPED, the stated reason names that the trail spans more than one piece of work.
All six decisions (R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R2.1, R2.2, R2.3) are accounted for: each appears either in '## Decisions' or is covered by the Out of scope entry. None vanishes without mention.
Provenance is assigned faithfully: R1.1, R1.2, R2.1, R2.2 are labelled ruled; R1.3 and R2.3 are labelled established.
assertions.leak: The fixture's trail JSON prints each entry's provenance word, so the ruled/established split is transcribable without the skill. Kept as regression cover; not a discriminator.

evals.name: already-graduated-rerun
evals.prompt: Read eval-4.md and do what it asks: make sure the spec issue exists.
evals.expected_output: The run reports the existing issue #9491 and files nothing; terminal ALREADY-GRADUATED, treated as a success.

assertions.text: OUTCOME.md names exactly one terminal and it is exactly the token ALREADY-GRADUATED (same closed set as 1.1).
No new issue is created. POSTED.md records nothing posted.
assertions.leak: The fixture's `graduate read` output prints state graduated and the issue number, so 'did not file a second' is readable straight off it.

assertions.text: The run reports the existing spec issue number, #9491.
assertions.leak: #9491 is printed verbatim in the fixture.

assertions.text: The run treats the outcome as a success rather than an error, a failure, or a problem to work around. Proposing to file a second spec anyway fails.

evals.name: map-source-dedup-near-match
evals.prompt: Read eval-5.md and do what it asks: get the work on this map specified.
evals.expected_output: The run judges #9312 a near-match rather than the same observation, files one spec naming it as a neighbour, and carries the map's out-of-scope entry forward.

assertions.text: OUTCOME.md names exactly one terminal and it is exactly the token SPEC-FILED (same closed set as 1.1).
The run judges #9312 to be a NEAR-MATCH rather than the same observation, and files its own spec. Declining to file on the strength of the dedup candidate fails.
assertions.leak: The fixture's #9312 body says 'Nothing here about conflicts — just batching', pre-answering the near-match judgement.

assertions.text: The filed spec names #9312 as a neighbouring issue so triage can merge them deliberately.
The run does not add its spec as a note or comment on #9312 instead of filing a new issue.
The map's recorded out-of-scope direction (operational transform for text fields) is carried into the spec's '## Out of scope' section or explicitly accounted for; it is not silently dropped.
assertions.leak: The map's outOfScope entry is printed in full in the trail JSON, so its content can be lifted directly.

assertions.text: Provenance is assigned faithfully: the ruled entry (ref `#9301 R1.2`, a session ruling relayed onto the map) is labelled ruled; #9507 and #9509 are labelled established.
assertions.leak: The fixture's trail JSON prints each entry's provenance word, so the ruled/established split is transcribable without the skill. Kept as regression cover; not a discriminator.
assertions.note: KEY DEFECT, found by the grader and fixed after the graded runs: this clause previously named #9505 as the ruled entry, a ref that no longer exists in the fixture — it was renumbered to #9301 R1.2 during the pre-run repair (a map TICKET cannot resolve to `ruled`; only a ## Decisions entry citing a session ruling can). Both arms were graded generously against the intent and passed. The graded runs therefore scored the old wording.

assertions.text: The run does not close or retire the map #9502.

The run does NOT copy #9312's labels (type:feature, p2, status:triaged) onto the new spec. The filed spec carries status:needs-triage and nothing else; proposing a type or priority because a neighbouring issue has one fails.
